title: Mark Cuban-backed group buys an A’s stake as investor picture grows a bit clearer
content:
As construction on the Athletics’ new ballpark in Las Vegas has progressed over the past year, owner John Fisher has more than once said he has sold pieces of the team to various investors. But Fisher has rarely offered details of a process that was intended to raise about $550 million.

Now, though, that rather murky picture is growing a bit clearer. At least three of the investment groups that have bought into the A’s have been identified publicly, including the latest on Thursday, which had a familiar name attached.

That group, Harbinger Sports Partners, is a private-equity firm dedicated to sports and backed by Mark Cuban, who gained fame as the owner of the NBA’s Dallas Mavericks and on the television show “Shark Tank.” Harbinger didn’t specify how much of the team it had acquired in its announcement of the transaction.

The firm, which was launched last year and said in April it had raised more than $450 million, was founded by Rashaun Williams, a limited partner in the NFL’s Atlanta Falcons, who also makes regular appearances on “Shark Tank.” Jonathan Mariner, formerly Major League Baseball’s chief financial officer, and Steve Cannon, a former Falcons executive, are principals as well.

Aramark, which will provide food and beverage services at the new A’s stadium, announced last year that it had acquired a piece of the team. And a Korean firm, Team 61, also has a slice of the club.

Chan Ho Park, a former big leaguer, and Suga, a member of the popular band BTS, are among Team 61’s investors, according to The Korea Economic Daily, which reported the firm owns about 2 to 3 percent of the team. Fisher confirmed in late 2025 that the A’s “have a group of Korean partners who’ve come in.”

Overall, the team has “raised a significant amount,” Fisher told The Athletic in June, adding that it was no longer courting investors.

“I won’t comment on numbers,” Fisher said then. “I was very happy and pleased with the group of people that we have joining us, and so we’ve put a pause on it for now.

“We did what we wanted to do, which we said was our goal, which was to bring in a significant number of local investors, so that this team would feel like a local team. We wanted to bring in some investors … globally, because we think that Las Vegas is a global town.”

Harbinger’s investment was agreed to prior to June, the A’s said, even though it only became public Thursday.

In a statement, the team said it was “very pleased” to add Harbinger to the mix: “The experience of their principals across sports, media, and entertainment, combined with their long-term perspective, makes them a valuable addition to our ownership group as we work to build the future of the franchise in Las Vegas.”

Private-equity groups have made a large foray into sports this decade, helping to drive up franchise values in a variety of leagues. Baseball teams, however, typically sell for less than their counterparts in the NBA or NFL.

The influx of funding for the A’s comes at a critical moment for Major League Baseball, which is mired in labor negotiations with a possible lockout looming. MLB owners hope that if they can land a salary cap in contentious talks with the players’ union — which would come with significant changes to revenue sharing and media rights — club valuations will improve.

“If you look at professional sports, I think investors now see that as a separate category of investments that is significant in terms of diversifying your overall portfolio,” MLB commissioner Rob Manfred said last week prior to the All-Star Game. “I also think that, particularly given some of the issues that we’re dealing with right now, people are thinking that the game could be on an upswing in terms of its investment potential.”

Last year, Fisher referenced the A’s former crosstown rivals, the San Francisco Giants, as a model the team looked to when courting investors.

“You’ve seen what the Giants have done in San Francisco, where they have lots of partners,” Fisher said in an interview with The Athletic last year. “What the Warriors have done, Golden State Warriors, I remember reading, I think, a New York Times Magazine story about their system, and how all the additional partners they brought in had made the team that much stronger.”

The A’s new stadium, which is projected to cost at least $2.1 billion, including about $380 million in taxpayer dollars, is scheduled to open in 2028. The team left Oakland after the 2024 season amidst controversy and is currently playing home games in Sacramento, Calif., in a minor-league ballpark.
